newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle returns to earth.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle returns to earth.

text.p: The U.S. space shuttle Columbia touched down at sunrise Thursday in Florida after completing a research mission cut short in April.
Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four shuttles, landed at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre at 6:46 a.m. EDT (1046 GMT) under the first rays of the morning sun.
Columbia's seven astronauts completed an $86 million research programme left unfinished in April, when the shuttle had to return to earth 12 days early because of a defective power generator.
It was the first time NASA had sent a shuttle and its crew back to space to complete a mission. Columbia was made ready for its second try in near-record time.
Since blasting off on July 1, Columbia's crew performed more than 30 experiments and ignited 206 controlled fires for combustion research, 42 more than originally planned.
"We've done better than anybody expected," mission scientist Michael Robinson said.
